newsitem.title: MOROCCO: King Hassan briefs delegation for W.Sahara talks.
newsitem.headline: King Hassan briefs delegation for W.Sahara talks.

text.p: Morocco's King Hassan on Sunday briefed officials who are to attend a Lisbon meeting on Monday with the U.N. leader's personal envoy on the Western Sahara, the official news agency MAP said.

The four-strong team, headed by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, will meet U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan's special emissary James Baker, said MAP without mentioning direct talks with Polisario leaders who have also been invited by Annan.
"During the meeting...King Hassan gave his highest instructions and enlightened guidance to the members of the delegation," said MAP.
Interior Minister Driss Basri and King Hassan's advisers Driss Slaoui and Andre Azoulay attended the meeting, MAP added.
U.N. Security Council members expressed satisfaction last Thursday that Morocco and the Polisario Front had agreed to hold direct talks in Portugal under the auspices of envoy James Baker.

Morocco claims the Western Sahara while the Polisario Front seeks an independent state there. Under a U.N. peace plan, a referendum was to have been held in January 1992 -- six months after a ceasefire came into force -- to enable the people of the territory to choose between independence and integration with Morocco.
The ballot has been bogged down in disputes over who should be eligible to vote.
